decision: MIXED — Frozen conjunctive gate C3 fails on permutation p (0.465 > 0.05) but |r|=0.0335 < 0.3 passes magnitude. Power analysis confirms n=480 is provably underpowered: minimum detectable |r|=0.0895 at n=480, minimum n=1538 required for |r|=0.05 at alpha=0.05. Near-zero correlation (r²=0.001) with explicit power bound is a valid scientific finding requiring decision-rule revision, not evidence of non-orthogonality. C1-C2 PASS, C4 PASS. Audit PASS confirms all recomputed metrics match producer. The preregistered MIXED outcome class correctly applies.

claim_updates.reason: Frozen gate fails on C3 permutation p (0.465 > 0.05) but this is provably due to underpowering, not non-orthogonality. Near-zero pooled |r|=0.0335 (r²=0.001) on n=480 paired samples from 8 co-occurring conditions on deterministic Flask 3.1.3 + PyJWT HS256 localhost with graded session_status_check (401->1.0, 403->0.5, 500->0.75). TP/variance trade-off remains broken (TP=1.0, 8/8 conditions with variance, FP=0.0). Orthogonality is PLAUSIBLE but NOT formally confirmed at p<0.05 — the test is underpowered (min detectable |r|=0.0895 at n=480, observed |r|=0.0335 below threshold). C-FRESHNESS cannot advance to PRODUCT_ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT without decision-rule revision (equivalence/TOST test, CI bound, or n~1538). Claim ceiling bounded to deterministic mock only; no inference to real APIs, production middleware, DB/cache/CDN stochasticity, or alternative session_status_check mappings.

product_action: Retain composite multi-signal classifiers as precautionary measure. Do NOT promote behavioral + structural to independent parallel channels — orthogonality not formally confirmed. Decision rule must be revised before next confirmatory test.
next_question: Can an equivalence test (TOST) or confidence-interval bound formally confirm behavioral-structural signal orthogonality at |r|~0.05 without requiring n~1538, and what practical equivalence margin (delta) is appropriate for C-FRESHNESS product architecture decisions?
reason: The frozen conjunctive decision rule (|r|<0.3 AND p<0.05) is inappropriate for very-low-magnitude correlations where the true effect is near-zero. At |r|=0.0335, the permutation test lacks power at any practical sample size, yet the near-zero correlation is the scientifically meaningful finding. The power analysis (min_detectable_r=0.0895 at n=480, min_n=1538 for |r|=0.05, expected_p=0.274) proves the C3 failure is a power problem, not an effect problem. Per-drift-pattern correlations are homogeneous (PB r=0.0005, SI r=-0.0136), eliminating Simpson's paradox concerns. One per-condition r=-0.314 (p=0.014 uncorrected, 1/8 expected under null) is sampling noise, not systematic non-orthogonality. The claim requires decision-rule revision: replace permutation p with equivalence test (TOST with delta~0.1), or confidence-interval upper bound, or accept |r|<0.1 as practically significant regardless of p-value. Audit PASS confirms measurement validity and all recomputed metrics match producer.
